transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Sentinel CISO), Liam O'Donnell (Head of Platform), Ravi Patel (Security Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Sentinel Bank run through encryption at rest/in transit, key management options (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, BYOK, Cloud HSM), HSM hardware requirements, audit logs, SOC2 considerations. Agreement to share SOC2, KMS integration docs and schedule follow-up for HSM deep dive + BYOK test plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, excuse me if audio is a bit off, we got priya and i from redwood here. who do we have on the sentinel side?
[00:08] Marta: hey jordan, this is marta reyes, ciso at sentinel, hi priya. liam and ravi are on as well.
[00:12] Liam: hi all.
[00:14] Ravi: morning.
[00:17] Jordan: great, quick agenda, go over encryption at rest and in transit, KMS options, BYOK flow and HSM support, and then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:24] Marta: yep that's perfect, our main goal is to understand if redwood can meet our key management and audit needs - we can't have customer data keys managed entirely by vendor without controls.
[00:33] Priya: understood. i'll start with a quick overview of options: hosted keys (Redwood-managed KMS), customer-managed KMS (CMEK/BYOK), and hardware-backed keys (HSM). we support standard providers like AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure key vault for CMEK. for HSM we integrate with cloud HSM or customer HSM via a supported import path.
[00:50] Ravi: when you say import path, do you support plaintext key import or a wrapped key envelope? we have strict rules, we need zero-knowledge, ideally wrapped key import with HSM attestation.
[00:58] Priya: yeah for BYOK we typically do a wrapped key import. the typical flow is you generate key material in your HSM or KMS, wrap it with a Redwood public key, then upload the wrapped blob. Redwood never sees unwrapped key material. we can also support importing via an offline key transfer if you need FIPS 140-2 validated procedures.
[01:18] Marta: do you have a diagram for the flow? audit trail? we need to show in our SOC2 that the vendor doesn't have key material.
[01:25] Jordan: i'll attach the BYOK flow diagram and the whitepaper. we also have an audit log for key import events - time, actor, IP - that we can surface via the Console and stream to your SIEM (splunk, sumo, etc.).
[01:36] Ravi: good. what about HSM-backed keys in dedicated mode - can the HSM live in our VPC and you call it over private connectivity, or does redwood require keys in your control plane?
[01:45] Priya: in Dedicated and Private deployments we support a customer-owned HSM in the VPC. the control plane can be private and we call out to the HSM via VPC peering or private link. we also offer a model where you manage keys in your cloud HSM (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) and we use a KMS proxy to perform crypto operations without exfiltrating Keys.
[02:05] Liam: latency wise, if every token invocation requires a remote HSM call that's going to add 50-200ms per request, can you cache key material?
[02:12] Priya: good question - we do not cache raw key material outside the HSM. what we do is cache a derived envelope or use symmetric wrapping keys inside the HSM to allow batched crypto operations. the runtime keeps short-lived wrappers (in memory) and we avoid round-trips for each token. for high-throughput workloads we recommend Dedicated with local HSM in the same region to minimize network hops.
[02:34] Ravi: that sounds reasonable, can you rotate keys? our policy is quarterly rotate with zero downtime.
[02:40] Priya: yes we support rotate with rolling rewrap. typical pattern: you create a new CMK in your HSM/KMS, wrap existing data keys to new CMK, we replay rewrap operations across caches. there is a short window but we can architect to have zero customer-perceived downtime; we'll provide a documented rotation runbook.
[02:58] Marta: what about key escrow, do you retain any copies for disaster recovery? we have a policy against vendor escrow.
[03:05] Jordan: we don't keep unwrapped key material for BYOK. for Redwood-managed keys we hold them encrypted in our KMS but we can do multi-tenant isolation and export logs. for customers with strict no-escrow we recommend customer-managed KMS where you control the master key.
[03:18] Ravi: compliance - FIPS 140-2, PCI, HIPAA, any certifications for your HSM integrations?
[03:25] Priya: our recommended path is to use cloud HSMs that are FIPS validated; Redwood itself does not claim HSM certification for customer-managed hardware, but the cloud providers' HSMs have the certs. for our control plane we support FIPS modes and we have SOC2 and ISO-27001 coverage - i'll attach the cert pack.
[03:40] Liam: can we get a copy of your SOC2 report redacted?
[03:43] Jordan: yes, we'll share our SOC2 type II and the relevant system description and the KMS whitepaper.
[03:47] Marta: what about audit logs - how long do you retain them and are they tamper-evident?
[03:52] Priya: default retention is 90 days in Console, but we can stream logs to your customer-owned S3 or SIEM for long-term retention and immutability. logs include KMS API calls, key import events, admin role changes. for tamper evidence we write an append-only digest and can provide periodic signed manifests.
[04:11] Ravi: does the log include the request payloads? some payloads may contain PII; we need redaction.
[04:16] Priya: we mask sensitive payload fields by default; full payload capture is optional but if you choose it we recommend streaming to your SIEM under your retention and access controls.
[04:25] Marta: access controls - how do you map our internal RBAC/SSO? we use SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning.
[04:31] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. you can map groups to roles and we enforce RBAC at route and token level. we also integrate with your audit identity provider so logs show the federated principal.
[04:42] Liam: can you do per-route keys? e.g., different key per customer namespace?
[04:46] Priya: yes per-tenant keys are supported; you can have a key per workspace, per route, whatever granularity you need. keys are scoped and the Console surfaces usage and the per-key billing if you want.
[04:58] Ravi: about encryption in transit - do you terminate TLS at redwood edge? what ciphers?
[05:03] Priya: we terminate TLS at the edge with latest ciphers, TLS1.2+, prefer TLS1.3, AES-GCM suites, ECDHE. for Private deployments you can front with your own TLS termination or use mutual TLS between your network and our endpoints.
[05:14] Marta: mutual TLS - do you support mTLS for ingest? we have strict egress rules, need client certs.
[05:19] Priya: yes mTLS is supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted API we use token-based auth and standard TLS. we can offer a private endpoint with mTLS for enterprise customers.
[05:29] Jordan: competitor question - some vendors claim they support BYOK but actually upload unwrapped keys, do you have attestation or a third-party audit?
[05:36] Priya: we have documented attestation steps and the wrap/unwrap flow is covered in our SOC2 controls; for high-security customers we can arrange an on-site/remote audit and share KMS configuration.
[05:45] Ravi: what about multi-region keys and data residency? if customer data must remain in eu, keys need to be EU-only.
[05:52] Priya: we support regional deployments. you can pin your model serving and KMS region. for EU-only residency we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated hosted in eu-west-1 with keys provisioned in that region's KMS.
[06:03] Liam: how does this affect latency - trying to balance cost and performance.
[06:06] Priya: routing policy can keep requests in region, we also recommend local HSM and Dedicated to keep latency minimal. cost tradeoff: Dedicated + HSM is more expensive but gives predictable latency and isolation.
[06:16] Marta: one more question on key rotation and audit - can we trigger rotation from our side or must it be done through Redwood Console?
[06:23] Priya: you can trigger rotation from your KMS (if CMEK) or via our API if you want us to orchestrate. we provide APIs and CLI for rotation workflows and will provide a runbook to meet your quarterly rotate requirement.
[06:33] Ravi: do you support split-key or Shamir's secret share for extra protection?
[06:37] Priya: we don't natively offer Shamir inside the platform but we can support split-key handled by your HSM and the wrapped-key import. essentially you can assemble the key in your HSM from shares, wrap it locally and then import.
[06:49] Jordan: at this point maybe worth briefly covering Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for security tradeoffs?
[06:54] Priya: sure - hosted is fastest to get started but vendor-managed keys. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and support for customer KMS and private networking. Private gives full customer control of control plane and optional on-prem components. For strict compliance (no vendor-managed keys, data residency) Private or Dedicated with customer KMS/HSM is the recommended path.
[07:14] Marta: sounds like Dedicated + customer managed KMS in our VPC is probably the minimum acceptable. we need to present this to legal and procurement.
[07:21] Liam: procurement will want pricing and SLA for HSM availability.
[07:24] Jordan: i'll include pricing options and our SLA matrix; priya can follow up on the integration specifics and runbook.
[07:31] Ravi: regarding HSM vendors, we prefer AWS CloudHSM or YubiHSM for on-prem, do you have experience with both?
[07:38] Priya: yes we've integrated with CloudHSM a lot; YubiHSM is supported for on-prem imports as a wrapped-key flow - we'll need to validate network connectivity and key import tooling.
[07:48] Marta: one red flag - do you store any customer PII in logs? we need to avoid that.
[07:53] Priya: PII is masked by default; any capture of request payloads is opt-in and we'd recommend streaming to your SIEM under your controls.
[08:01] Jordan: ok, wrapping up, quick recap of next steps and owners...
[08:05] Priya: i'll run the HSM integration deep dive with ravi and liam - propose week of 11/9.
[08:10] Jordan: i'll send the SOC2 pack, KMS BYOK whitepaper, and Dedicated + HSM pricing by 11/5.
[08:15] Ravi: i'll share the network diagram and compliance contact by 11/4.
[08:19] Marta: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:21] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[08:24] (meeting ends)
